tagline: The Birkin waitlist, the Chanel price hikes, and bags as a currency.
why: Luxury handbags are the core of the fashion business and, for some models, an asset class. A Hermès Birkin can cost more on the resale market than in the store, and Chanel's classic flap has risen in price many times over. In Hong Kong, bags are a highly visible status signal and a big resale industry, so bag talk is everywhere: at work, among friends and on social media.

essentials.title: The hierarchy
essentials.body: Hermès sits at the top, then Chanel. Louis Vuitton, Dior, Celine, Loewe, Bottega Veneta, Prada and Goyard follow. Quiet brands like The Row are the connoisseur's choice.

essentials.title: Hermès plays hard to get
essentials.body: You can't simply buy a Birkin or Kelly. Sales associates offer them to clients with a strong purchase history, a practice people call 'the game'.

essentials.title: Classics hold value
essentials.body: Iconic models like the Birkin, Kelly, Chanel Classic Flap and LV Speedy hold value better than seasonal 'it-bags'.

essentials.title: Leathers and hardware matter
essentials.body: Collectors talk about leathers (Togo, Epsom, caviar, lambskin), sizes (Birkin 25, 30, 35) and hardware (gold or palladium).

essentials.title: Resale is a big market
essentials.body: Pre-owned shops and platforms authenticate and resell bags. Condition, box and receipt affect price.

essentials.title: Fakes are a huge issue
essentials.body: 'Superfakes' are hard to spot, which is why authentication services and trusted dealers matter.

names.name: Hermès
names.what: The most exclusive maker, every bag hand-made by a single artisan.

names.name: Chanel
names.what: The Classic Flap and Boy bag; prices have risen dramatically since 2019.

names.name: Louis Vuitton
names.what: The Speedy, Neverfull and Keepall; the monogram is the most recognised pattern in luxury.

names.name: Dior
names.what: The Lady Dior (named after Princess Diana) and the Saddle bag.

names.name: Goyard
names.what: Discreet French trunk-maker; its chevron tote is loved by Hong Kong professionals.

names.name: Bottega Veneta
names.what: Woven leather and no logos; the Jodie and Cassette bags.

names.name: Loewe
names.what: The Puzzle bag made the Spanish house a favourite.

names.name: Celine
names.what: The Triomphe and the old Luggage tote; the 'quiet' choice.

names.name: The Row
names.what: Mary-Kate and Ashley Olsen's brand; its Margaux bag is the quiet luxury status bag.

names.name: Miu Miu
names.what: Prada's sister brand; its bags are a hot item with younger buyers.

names.name: Jane Birkin
names.what: The actress who inspired the Birkin in 1984 after a chance meeting with Hermès's boss on a plane.

names.name: Milan Station
names.what: Hong Kong's well-known pre-owned luxury bag retailer.

timeline.event: Grace Kelly is photographed with the Hermès bag later named after her.
The Lady Dior is named after Princess Diana.
The era of it-bags, from Fendi Baguette to Balenciaga City.
Chanel raises Classic Flap prices repeatedly.
Jane Birkin dies; her original Birkin later sells for about €8.6 million at auction in 2025.

now.headline: The Birkin lawsuit
now.detail: A 2024 US lawsuit accused Hermès of tying Birkin sales to other purchases, putting 'the game' in the headlines.

now.headline: Price fatigue
now.detail: Some buyers balk at Chanel and LV prices, boosting interest in quieter brands and pre-owned bags.

now.headline: Pre-owned boom
now.detail: Second-hand luxury keeps growing, and brands themselves are entering resale.

now.headline: Bag charms
now.detail: Decorating bags with charms and plush toys, like Labubu, became a big trend in 2025.

local.headline: Resale capital
local.detail: Hong Kong has a large pre-owned bag market, from Milan Station to boutique dealers and auction houses.

local.headline: Auctions
local.detail: Christie's Hong Kong handbag auctions regularly set records for rare Hermès pieces.

local.headline: Where people shop
local.detail: Hermès at Pacific Place, Landmark and Harbour City; Chanel and LV flagships in Central and TST.

local.headline: Labubu craze
local.detail: Pop Mart's Labubu, created by Hong Kong-born artist Kasing Lung, became a global bag-charm phenomenon.

debates.question: Are bags an investment?
debates.sides: Hermès classics have held value; most other bags don't. Buy to use, not to flip.

debates.question: Is 'the game' fair?
debates.sides: Hermès says it rewards loyal clients; critics say it's manipulative.

debates.question: Pre-owned or new?
debates.sides: Pre-owned is cheaper and more sustainable; new comes with the store experience.

debates.question: Logo or no logo?
debates.sides: Monograms are classic; quiet luxury fans prefer no branding.
